customManagers.description: Bump the Go tools the Makefile builds under .tools, each marked with a 'renovate:' comment on the line above its pin. Go module tags carry the v the Makefile writes, so the matched value is reused as is.

The linter version ci.yml hands the reusable lint workflow. Matched on the input's own name rather than a marker comment so the workflow file stays untouched, and grouped with the Makefile pin below so the two never disagree.

packageRules.description: Every bump lands as 'build' so it appears under the Dependencies changelog section, which release-please treats as releasable: a bumped module, action or base image is a new binary or image, and it reaches nobody without a release.
Non-major Go module bumps land together: one commit and one patch release a week rather than one per module. A vulnerable module skips both the grouping and the schedule through the OSV alerts above.
The linter is pinned twice on purpose - the Makefile for `make lint`, ci.yml for the reusable workflow - so a finding here is a finding there. One pull request moves both.
The Go toolchain is the go directive in go.mod, which CI reads through go-version-file, and the golang image both Dockerfiles build in. One pull request moves both.
Reusable workflows are called at the moving v0 major tag on purpose until github-workflows reaches v1 - don't pin or bump them.
